newsitem.title: INDIA: Oman says natural gas pipeline not feasible.
newsitem.headline: Oman says natural gas pipeline not feasible.

text.p: Omani Commerce Minister Makboul Ali Bin Sultan said on Thursday a $4 billion Oman-India subsea natural gas pipeline project did not appear feasible at present on technical and other considerations.
"I hope it will happen but I am not very optimistic," Makboul told a meeting of the Federation of Indian Commerce and Industry.
Makboul said the project required $10 billion in investments and submarines were needed to maintain it.
He said Oman had contacted most of the big oil companies and consultants but no one had really come forward to join in the project.
He said the Gulf state has spent $70 million to 80 million on the feasibility study for the project.

"Things are still not clear. The technical study and the guarantees required by Oman for $10 billion all show that the project today is not feasible. We have a committee looking at all this," Makboul said.
India said on Wednesday that the project had been put on hold in the absence of proper technology.
"For the time being...we are keeping it in abeyance till the technology is available," Indian Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral told reporters.
The two countries signed a memorandum of understanding in 1993 to build a pipeline between the two nations under the Arabian Sea.
A Foreign Ministry spokesman said earlier this month that the two governments had decided in 1996 to set up a joint committee of experts to study whether the project was feasible.
According to the original plan, the proposed pipeline would be more than 1,300 km (813 miles) long and lie up to two miles under the ocean's surface.

Makboul invited Indian private entrepreuners to invest in Oman and wanted the private sector from both countries to work together to translate into action the agreements signed by the two countries on investments and other areas.
